Kevin Trudeau says the oil hiding in your peanut butter jar is the same one that's a problem everywhere else.

Hydrogenated oil is a trans fat. His description of what it does: it scars the inside of your artery, which gives cholesterol something to grab onto and attach to the artery wall.

Kevin's list of what follows - messed-up hormones, a bigger appetite, and for some people, a lower mood.

The check is simple. Flip the label over. If it says 'hydrogenated oil' or 'partially hydrogenated,' that's the trans fat Kevin is talking about.

#kevintrudeau #wbdaily #transfat #readthelabel #foodtruth #healthtruth

Kevin Trudeau says there's one simple check before anything goes in your cart: does the label say 'No GMOs'?

If it does, he says you can be reasonably sure most of the ingredients weren't genetically modified. If that phrase is nowhere on the package, Kevin's rule is blunt - assume it's in there.

He brings up a guest from his radio show who once spent an hour and a half listing symptoms he linked to genetically modified food: bloating, colon trouble, hormone problems, extra fat, feeling foggy and spacey.

Kevin's advice is the same one his guest gave: read for the words 'No GMOs' before anything else on the label.

#kevintrudeau #wbdaily #gmo #readthelabel #foodtruth #healthtruth

Kevin Trudeau says to flip the bag before you reach for more Doritos.

If the label lists monosodium glutamate, MSG, that's what he calls an excitotoxin, in the same category as artificial sweeteners. His claim: it affects your neurotransmitters and makes you crave more of whatever you're already eating.

Kevin says companies add it because it keeps you coming back to the bag. He names Kentucky Fried Chicken and Taco Bell as two places loaded with it, on top of the hydrogenated oil and GMO corn already in the mix.

His line: no wonder you're fat, stressed and anxious, and never quite sure why.

#kevintrudeau #wbdaily #msg #readthelabel #foodtruth #fastfood

Kevin Trudeau says the wheat problem isn't the wheat - it's the clock.

His claim: wheat grown in Canada and America is typically fermented for only around 8 hours before it becomes bread, against roughly 48 hours for traditional wheat in places like Italy. He says that shorter fermentation is what leaves people gassy, bloated and reaching for more.

Kevin's workaround at his own table: pasta labeled 'product of Italy,' made from durum wheat fermented the longer way. His claim - no gas, no bloating, no cravings afterward, even for guests who normally react to wheat.

You can't always pick where your bread was made. You can start checking where your pasta was.

#kevintrudeau #wbdaily #wheat #readthelabel #foodtruth #italy

Kevin Trudeau says to be suspicious the moment a bottle calls itself 'organic soybean oil.'

His reasoning: nobody makes real salad dressing with soybean oil at home - the classic choice is extra virgin olive oil. So when a company reaches for soybean oil instead, Kevin's read is simple: it's cheap, and that's the only reason it's in the bottle.

He adds that almost all soy today comes from Monsanto seed and has been genetically modified, and that he links it to lower testosterone - organic label or not.

If soybean oil is listed ahead of olive oil, Kevin's advice is to put it back on the shelf.

#kevintrudeau #wbdaily #soy #readthelabel #foodtruth #healthtruth

Kevin Trudeau says cows are vegetarians by nature - they eat grass.

His claim about commercial beef: some cattle feed includes ground-up dead and diseased animals that couldn't legally be sold for meat anywhere else, mixed in to help cattle gain weight faster before slaughter.

Kevin's chain of reasoning: a sick animal's remains go into another animal's feed, that animal is also given growth hormone and antibiotics, and all of it ends up on a plate simply labeled 'beef.'

His rule for his own table: know what the animal that becomes your dinner was actually fed.

#kevintrudeau #wbdaily #beef #foodtruth #readthelabel #healthtruth

Kevin Trudeau says you don't have to fear beef and dairy - you just have to know what to look for.

His rule for beef: 100 percent grass-fed, organic, no antibiotics, no growth hormone - and he says you can eat as much of that as you want.

For cheese, Kevin's own choice is raw cheese, usually from France or Switzerland, made from cows that actually graze on grass. His sign of the real thing: unhomogenized milk where the cream naturally separates and rises to the top within a few days.

If your milk never separates, Kevin's question is simple - what did they do to stop it?
